title: Custom Sort String
description:
You are given two strings `order` and `s`. All the characters of `order` are **unique** and were sorted in some custom order previously.

Permute the characters of `s` so that they match the order that `order` was sorted. More specifically, if a character `x` occurs before a character `y` in `order`, then every occurrence of `x` should occur before every occurrence of `y` in the permuted string.

Characters in `s` that do not appear in `order` can be placed at any position. Return **any** permutation of `s` that satisfies this property. The judge validates that your returned string is a permutation of `s` and respects the relative order defined by `order` (`true`).
constraints: order and s consist of lowercase English letters.
All the characters of order are unique.
hints: You can sort the characters of s using a custom comparator that maps each character in order to its index (and unranked characters to 26).
For an even faster O(n + m) solution, count the frequency of each character in s using an array of size 26.
Iterate through order and append each character as many times as it appears in s, then append all remaining characters that were not in order.

examples.explanation: Characters 'c', 'b', and 'a' appear in order as c -> b -> a, so "cbad" (or "dcba", "cdba", etc.) is valid.
'b', 'c', and 'a' must appear in that relative order; 'd' is not in order and can go anywhere, e.g. "bcad".
Following order "kqep", the permutation "kqeep" places 'k', 'q', both 'e's, then 'p'.

inputs.name: order
inputs.description: Unique lowercase characters defining the custom rank order
